# Why surveydown?

Your project lives or dies on its survey. Every choice model we estimate later
in the semester is only as good as the data the survey collects. The usual tools
(Google Forms, Qualtrics) are point-and-click: nothing is reproducible, the data
sits on someone else's server, and the features you need for conjoint — random
designs, conditional logic, custom display — are limited or paywalled.

[surveydown](https://surveydown.org/) flips that. **A survey is code**: a Quarto
document for the content, an R script for the app, and a PostgreSQL database you
control for the responses. Because it's plain text, it can be version controlled,
shared, and — importantly for us — written and edited by an agent.

| | Google Forms | surveydown |
|------|:---:|:---:|
| Reproducible | no | yes |
| You control the data | no | yes |
| Free & open source | partly | yes |
| Conjoint-ready | no | yes |

# The two files

Every survey is a folder with two files that work together:

| File | What it defines |
|------|-----------------|
| `survey.qmd` | Content: pages, text, images, questions |
| `app.R` | The Shiny app: database, server logic, launch |

```{=typst}
#keypoint[
  **Content goes in `survey.qmd`; logic goes in `app.R`.** Questions and pages are
  *defined* in the Quarto doc. Anything that *decides* what a respondent sees
  (showing, skipping, stopping, reacting to answers) goes inside the `server()`
  function in `app.R`.
]
```

## A minimal survey.qmd

````markdown
---
survey-settings:
  mode: preview
---

```{r}
library(surveydown)
```

--- welcome

# Welcome to our survey!

```{r}
sd_question(
  type   = "mc",
  id     = "penguins",
  label  = "What's your favorite penguin?",
  option = c(
    "Adélie"    = "adelie",
    "Chinstrap" = "chinstrap",
    "Gentoo"    = "gentoo"
  )
)
```

--- end

```{r}
sd_close()
```
````

- **Pages** start with three dashes and a page id (`--- welcome`). No closing
  tag: the next page marker ends the page.
- A **Next** button is added to every page automatically.
- `sd_close()` on the last page adds an "Exit Survey" button.

## The standard app.R

```r
library(surveydown)

db <- sd_db_connect()     # connect to database
ui <- sd_ui()             # standard UI

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # conditional logic / reactivity goes here
  sd_server(db)
}

shiny::shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

Run it with the **Run App** arrow at the top of `app.R`. surveydown doesn't
always pick up saved edits while running — stop the app and run it again.

## Starting a new survey

```r
surveydown::sd_create_survey(
  template = "default",
  path = "path/to/my-survey"
)
```

**Every survey gets its own folder.** Browse the
[templates](https://surveydown.org/templates), or build visually with the
[studio app](https://sdstudio.surveydown.org/) via `sdstudio::launch()`.

# Survey basics

## YAML settings

All settings live in the YAML header of `survey.qmd`. No header means all
defaults. Full list on the
[Survey Settings](https://surveydown.org/docs/survey-settings) page.

| Key | What it does |
|-----|--------------|
| `mode` | Where responses are saved (below) |
| `show-previous` | `yes` adds a Previous button |
| `all-required` | `yes` makes every question required |
| `required` | List of specific required question ids |
| `theme` | Any [bootswatch](https://bootswatch.com/) theme name |
| `barcolor` | Progress bar color |
| `barposition` | `top`, `bottom`, or `none` |

`mode`, `show-previous`, and the required keys go under `survey-settings`; the
theme and bar keys go under `theme-settings`. Custom styling:
`theme: [united, custom.scss]`.

| `mode` | Responses saved to |
|--------|--------------------|
| `preview` | `preview_data.csv` in the folder |
| `local` | `local_data.csv` in the folder |
| `database` | Your database (the default) |

**Build in `preview`, launch in `database`.**

## Questions

```r
sd_question(
  type   = "mc",
  id     = "fruit",
  label  = "1. Do you like fruit?",
  option = c(
    "Yes!"    = "yes",
    "Kind of" = "kind_of",
    "No :("   = "no"
  )
)
```

Options are written `"Label" = "value"`: respondents see the label, your data
stores the value. The `id` becomes the column name in your data, so keep it short
and unique.

| Type | What it is |
|------|------------|
| `mc` | Multiple choice, pick one |
| `mc_multiple` | Multiple choice, pick many |
| `mc_buttons` | Pick one, large buttons |
| `select` | Drop-down menu |
| `text` | One line of open text |
| `textarea` | Block of open text |
| `numeric` | Numbers only |
| `matrix` | Many items, same options (Likert) |

More on the [question types](https://surveydown.org/docs/question-types) page.

**Or define questions in `questions.yml`** — the same fields as YAML, keyed by
id — then call `sd_question("fruit")` in `survey.qmd`. See `demo-questions-yml`.

## Navigation and images

- `sd_nav(label_next = "Continue")` changes one page's buttons.
- Images: plain html is the most predictable —
  `<img src="logo.png" width=250>` inside a `<center>` tag.

# Conditional logic

Three functions, all placed in `server()` in `app.R`. Each takes one or more
formulas of the form *condition* `~` *"target_id"*.

| Function | If the condition is TRUE… |
|----------|---------------------------|
| `sd_show_if()` | **Show** a question or page |
| `sd_skip_if()` | **Skip** ahead to a page |
| `sd_stop_if()` | **Stop** navigation, with a message |

Use `sd_value("id")` to read a respondent's answer.

## Show a follow-up question

```r
sd_show_if(
  sd_value("penguins") == "other" ~ "penguins_other"
)
```

Both questions are defined in `survey.qmd`; the target stays hidden until the
condition is met. `sd_is_answered("id")` is another handy condition.

## Randomly show one of two pages

```r
rand_val <- sample(c("A", "B"), 1)
sd_store_value(rand_val)   # record which version
sd_show_if(
  rand_val == "A" ~ "page2a",
  rand_val == "B" ~ "page2b"
)
```

`sd_store_value()` saves the draw in your data, so you know which version each
respondent saw. This is the seed of conjoint randomization.

## Screen out a respondent

```r
sd_skip_if(
  sd_value("vehicle_ownership") == "no" ~ "screenout"
)
```

…with a `--- screenout` page in `survey.qmd` saying they don't qualify.

# Storing data

Responses go to any **PostgreSQL** database. We use
[Supabase](https://supabase.com/) (free, open source). Full details on the
[Storing Data](https://surveydown.org/docs/storing-data) page.

1. Create a Supabase account and a project (the project is your database;
   choose a strong password).
2. Click **Connect**, choose **Direct**, and find the **Transaction pooler**
   section for your credentials.
3. Run `surveydown::sd_db_config()` in the console and enter them. They're saved
   in a `.env` file in your survey folder.
4. Set `mode: database` in `survey.qmd` (or delete the `mode` line).
5. `sd_db_connect()` in `app.R` reads `.env` and connects.

**Never share or commit `.env`** — it holds your database password. View your
responses locally with `sdstudio::launch()`.

# Reactivity

Reactivity means **changing something based on respondent input**. For the
general idea read the
[Mastering Shiny chapter](https://mastering-shiny.org/basic-reactivity.html);
for surveydown, the [reactivity page](https://surveydown.org/docs/reactivity).

The easy way is `sd_output()` in `survey.qmd`, no server code needed:

| `type =` | Displays (for the penguin question) |
|----------|-------------------------------------|
| `"value"` | The stored value: adelie |
| `"label_option"` | The chosen label: Adélie |
| `"label_question"` | The question text |

Drop it into text as inline R, e.g. *Hello,* `` `r sd_output("name", type = "value")` ``.

The full way is Shiny: put `output$greeting <- renderText({...})` in `server()`
and `textOutput("greeting")` in `survey.qmd`. `renderText()` re-runs every time
the name answer changes.

# Having an agent build a survey

Because a survey is just two text files, an agent can write the whole thing. Be
specific in your prompt — topic, question types, number of pages, conditional
logic — and point it at [surveydown.org](https://surveydown.org/) so it uses
the real functions. Then **verify it yourself**; "done" from an agent is a
claim, not a fact:

- Run the app and click through **every** page.
- Trigger each branch of the conditional logic, not just the default path.
- Check each `id` is short, unique, and means something in your data.
- Open `preview_data.csv` and confirm every question landed in a column.
- Broken or wrong? Describe what you saw and have it fix that.

# Errors you will hit

| Symptom | Usual cause |
|---------|-------------|
| Edits don't appear | App still running old version; stop & re-run |
| Can't connect to database | No `.env`; run `sd_db_config()` |
| No data in database | Still in `mode: preview` |
| Conditional logic ignored | Condition written in `survey.qmd`, not `app.R` |
| Question never shows | Target id typo in the formula |
| Paths break | Opened a file, not the survey folder |
